parakeet: If you stop believing, would you still be a good person? If your only reason for being a good person is God, what does that actually say about you? Because if your consciousness disappears without God, then did you ever really have one? Or were you just following orders? Think about it. If a person only does the right thing because they fear punishment or hope for reward, is that morality or is that obedience? Because true morality isn't about checking a box for heaven or avoiding hellfire. It's about promoting human well-being and not causing harm, even when no one is watching. And the irony, some of the most religious peoples, the ones who claim their faith gives them superior morals, have done some of the most horrific things in history. Slavery justified by scripture. Witch trials and burnings carried out in God's name and justified by scripture. Colonization and genocide, blessed by the church and justified by scripture. Clergy sex abuse scandals covered up by the very people preaching righteousness. So I'll ask again if religion guarantees morality, then why does history tell a different story? Why does every religion have testimonies of changed lives?
